== Biography ==
George Mark Glasgow, Esq. was likely born between 1790 and 1805 in the British Isles—possibly in England or Ireland. He served as a captain in the Royal Artillery, where he appears to have held a reputable position.

George married and had at least one daughter, Madeline Glasgow. By 1846, he had died (records call him “the late George Mark Glasgow”), and Madeline married George Nevile, Esq., of Stubton, Lincolnshire. Her advantageous marriage into the Nevile family—prominent in Lincolnshire—suggests George Mark Glasgow moved in higher social or military circles. Specific details about his career, personal life, and exact death information remain unknown.

== Research Notes ==
George Nevile, Esq. (b. 1822), the husband of Madeline Glasgow, was the youngest son of Rev. Henry William Nevile (Rector of Cottesmore, Rutland) and Amelia Mann of Hallow Park, near Worcester. He served as:
* High Sheriff of Lincolnshire (1858)  
* Justice of the Peace (J.P.)  
* Deputy Lieutenant (D.L.)  

Nevile inherited estates from Sir Robert Heron, 2nd Baronet (ext.), indicating deep family connections in both Lincolnshire and Nottinghamshire. This highlights that Madeline’s family—through her father, Capt. George Mark Glasgow—was linked to notable landowning and clerical families in the region.


* May be the same person as [[Glasgow-1536|George Glasgow (abt.1804–)]]

=== George Mark Glasgow, Royal Artillery appointments ===

A February 1825 notice names George Mark Glasgow as a First Lieutenant of the Royal Regiment of Artillery returning from half-pay. An Office of Ordnance notice dated 16 January 1837, reported on 24 January, names First Lieutenant George Mark Glasgow appointed Second Captain. Full name, corps and rank progression support career continuity, although neither notice supplies parents or a household.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050087237/ Freeman’s Journal, 1825-02-16, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390543080/ Belfast News-Letter, 24 January 1837, p. 1 (Office of Ordnance list dated 16 January)].</ref>

The exact full name and Royal Artillery career make this a strong compatible officer identification. [[Glasgow-3785|George Mark Glasgow]], born in Quebec in 1795 and reported dead in Kingston in 1851, remains a true rival; his 1851 death conflicts with the account of Madeline’s father being late by her 1846 marriage. [[Glasgow-1536|George Glasgow of Barony]] is a weaker proposed identity. These may not all be joined to one career without original service and family evidence.
